subsection.title: A locus example: perpendicular bisectors
subsection.p: A locus is a set of points satisfying a condition.
For example, the perpendicular bisector of a segment is the set of all points equidistant from the segment’s endpoints.

note.title: Why squared distances are allowed
note.p: Distance is nonnegative. If two distances are equal, then their squares are equal. Conversely, if two nonnegative distances have equal squares, then the distances are equal.
